questions.text: Karan's capital on 1 April is Rs. 6,50,000 and stays unchanged through the year. Interest on capital is allowed @ 7% p.a. Interest on Karan's capital for the year is:
questions.explanation: IOC = 650000 x 7% = Rs. 45,500  Correct option B. Distractors: A = forgot to divide the rate by 100; C = used 9% instead of 7%; D = charged interest for only half the year.

questions.text: On 1 April Esha's capital was Rs. 7,50,000. Esha introduced further capital of Rs. 1,00,000 on 1 July. Interest on capital is allowed @ 11% p.a. Interest on Esha's capital for the year is:
questions.explanation: Rs. 7,50,000 for 3 mo + Rs. 8,50,000 for 9 mo IOC = Rs. 90,750  Correct option A. Distractors: B = counted the elapsed months, not the remaining months; C = ignored the additional capital; D = treated the addition as brought in for the whole year.

questions.text: Karan's capital on 1 April was Rs. 2,50,000. Karan permanently withdrew Rs. 50,000 of capital on 1 December. Interest on capital is allowed @ 7% p.a. Interest on Karan's capital for the year is:
questions.explanation: Rs. 2,50,000 for 8 mo + Rs. 2,00,000 for 4 mo IOC = Rs. 16,333  Correct option C. Distractors: A = counted the elapsed months, not the remaining months; B = ignored the capital withdrawn; D = treated the reduced capital as the balance all year.

questions.text: Ishan began the year with capital of Rs. 5,50,000, introduced Rs. 50,000 on 1 July and withdrew Rs. 50,000 on 1 December. Interest on capital is allowed @ 7% p.a. Interest on Ishan's capital for the year is:
questions.explanation: product method over three balances; IOC = Rs. 39,958  Correct option D. Distractors: A = ignored the addition; B = ignored the withdrawal; C = ignored both movements.

questions.text: Karan's capital on 1 April is Rs. 6,00,000 and stays unchanged through the year. Interest on capital is allowed @ 7% p.a. Interest on Karan's capital for the year is:
questions.explanation: IOC = 600000 x 7% = Rs. 42,000  Correct option D. Distractors: A = charged interest for only half the year; B = used 9% instead of 7%; C = forgot to divide the rate by 100.

questions.text: On 1 April Chetan's capital was Rs. 9,00,000. Chetan introduced further capital of Rs. 1,00,000 on 1 December. Interest on capital is allowed @ 11% p.a. Interest on Chetan's capital for the year is:
questions.explanation: Rs. 9,00,000 for 8 mo + Rs. 10,00,000 for 4 mo IOC = Rs. 1,02,667  Correct option A. Distractors: B = treated the addition as brought in for the whole year; C = ignored the additional capital; D = counted the elapsed months, not the remaining months.

questions.text: Arun's capital on 1 April was Rs. 9,00,000. Arun permanently withdrew Rs. 50,000 of capital on 1 August. Interest on capital is allowed @ 7% p.a. Interest on Arun's capital for the year is:
questions.explanation: Rs. 9,00,000 for 4 mo + Rs. 8,50,000 for 8 mo IOC = Rs. 60,667  Correct option C. Distractors: A = treated the reduced capital as the balance all year; B = counted the elapsed months, not the remaining months; D = ignored the capital withdrawn.

questions.text: Ishan began the year with capital of Rs. 2,50,000, introduced Rs. 50,000 on 1 August and withdrew Rs. 50,000 on 1 January. Interest on capital is allowed @ 7% p.a. Interest on Ishan's capital for the year is:
questions.explanation: product method over three balances; IOC = Rs. 18,958  Correct option A. Distractors: B = ignored the withdrawal; C = ignored both movements; D = ignored the addition.

questions.text: Esha's capital on 1 April is Rs. 9,00,000 and stays unchanged through the year. Interest on capital is allowed @ 9% p.a. Interest on Esha's capital for the year is:
questions.explanation: IOC = 900000 x 9% = Rs. 81,000  Correct option B. Distractors: A = used 11% instead of 9%; C = forgot to divide the rate by 100; D = charged interest for only half the year.

questions.text: On 1 April Karan's capital was Rs. 9,00,000. Karan introduced further capital of Rs. 1,00,000 on 1 August. Interest on capital is allowed @ 15% p.a. Interest on Karan's capital for the year is:
questions.explanation: Rs. 9,00,000 for 4 mo + Rs. 10,00,000 for 8 mo IOC = Rs. 1,45,000  Correct option B. Distractors: A = counted the elapsed months, not the remaining months; C = ignored the additional capital; D = treated the addition as brought in for the whole year.
